data: 港[みなと]に 3[さん]隻[せき]の 船[ふね]が 停泊[ていはく] していた。
There were three ships anchored in the port.
Counter,Somewhat Common
隻 · せき · Big ships. Small boats use 艘 (そう).
この 家[いえ]には 寝室[しんしつ]が ３[さん] 部屋[へや] あります。
There are three bedrooms in this house.
Counter,Common
部屋 · へや · Rooms. For one, two, and sometimes three rooms, use the wago counting method. Beyond that use kango.
その 年[とし]は、 ５[ご]行[ぎょう]の 銀行[ぎんこう]が 倒産[とうさん] した。
That year five banks went bankrupt.
Counter,Somewhat Common
行 · こう · Banks, groups of people, parties of people.
お好[この]み焼[や]き ソースを 2[に] 刷毛[はけ] 塗[ぬ]った。
I smeared on two strokes of okonomiyaki sauce.
Counter,Somewhat Common
刷毛 · はけ · Brush strokes.
そこの 狭[せま]い 道[みち]を 入[はい]って 右側[みぎがわ]に ありますよ。
It's on the right side when you go into that narrow street over there.
鼠,Travel
お金[かね]を 入[い]れたんですが、 切符[きっぷ]が 出[で]ません。
I put money in, but the ticket didn’t come out.
Travel

"お金を入れたんですが" means "I put in the money, but..." The verb "入れる" (ireru) means "to put in," and "お金" (okane) means "money." The "たんですが" at the end adds a nuance of explanation or reason, similar to saying "but..." in English. "切符が出ません" means "the ticket is not coming out." "切符" (kippu) means "ticket," and "出ません" (demasen) is the negative form of the verb "出る" (deru), meaning "to come out" or "to be dispensed."
この 病院[びょういん]には 今[いま] 3[さん]床[しょう]しか 空[あ]きが ありません。
This hospital has only three available beds at the moment.
Counter,Somewhat Common
床 · しょう · Hospital beds, clinic beds, cots, rafts, false teeth.
ビエトから 金[きん] 1[いち] 封[ふう]と 書[か]いた 封筒[ふうとう]を 渡[わた]された。
Viet gave me an envelope that says "sealed money."
Counter,Somewhat Common
封 · ふう · Envelopes of money and sealed letters in envelopes.
コウイチの デスクの 下[した]に 小豆[あずき]が ３[さん] 粒[つぶ] 落[お]ちていた。
There were three adzuki beans underneath Koichi's desk.
Counter,Common
粒 · つぶ · Small, round things—usually quite small. Think in terms of little things you can pile up and collect in a jar or other container.
あなたと 一緒[いっしょ]に いたい 女性[じょせい] （男性[だんせい]）は たくさん いるよ。
There are lots of women (men) who would love to be with you.
Emotion
高級[こうきゅう] 時計[とけい] ５[ご]点[てん]が 盗[ぬす]まれた。
We had five high-end watches stolen.
Counter,Common

点 · てん · Items, scores, dots, points, fulcrums, and any kind of artwork including paintings, sculptures, literature, and even films. When counting scores, 点 can be applicable to the score of a sports game as well as your score on a test.
彼女[かのじょ]は 最高[さいこう]の 恋人[こいびと]だったのに。
She was the best girlfriend I ever had.
Emotion
あなたは 自分[じぶん]の 感情[かんじょう]を 押[お]し付[つ]ける。
You're always imposing yourself on other people.
Emotion
３[さん]泊[ぱく] ４日[よっか]で 東京[とうきょう] 旅行[りょこう]に 行[い]ってきた。
I went on a three-night and four-day trip to Tokyo.
Counter,Common
泊 · はく · Overnight stays or rentals.
私[わたし]の 気持[きも]ちは 彼[かれ] （彼女[かのじょ]）に 届[とど]かない。
He (she) doesn't have the same feelings for me as I have for him (her).
Emotion
あの 選手[せんしゅ]は、 1[いち] 試合[しあい]で 合計[ごうけい] 7[なな]盗[とう] した。
That player stole seven bases in one game.
Counter,Somewhat Common
盗 · とう · Steals (of bases) in baseball.
一緒[いっしょ]に 5[ご]重[じゅう]の 塔[とう]を 見[み]に 行[い]きませんか？
Do you wanna go see the five-story pagoda with me?
Counter,Somewhat Common
重 · じゅう · Things that overlap with one another, including overlapped layers and repetitive actions. To count layers that don't overlap, we usually use the counter 層 (そう).
生[う]まれ変[か]わったら 今度[こんど]は 一緒[いっしょ]に なろう。
Let's be together in our next life.
Emotion
今[いま]まで 一番[いちばん] 辛[つら]かった 経験[けいけん]を 話[はな]して。
Tell me about your worst experience.
Emotion
受付[うけつけ]に お約束[やくそく]の 御[ご]２[に] 方[ほう]が お見[み]えです。
There are two people in reception who have an appointment.
Counter,Somewhat Common
方 · かた · People (formal). For one, two, and three people, you'll want to attach the prefix 御 (お). You can also refer to a group of people of an unknown number using 方.
神[かみ]様[さま] お願[ねが]い、 もう 一度[いちど] 彼[かれ] （彼女[かのじょ]）と 会[あ]わせて。
Please, God, let me see him (her) again.
Emotion
お土産[みやげ]に、 お茶[ちゃ] 菓子[かし] 14[じゅうよん] 包[つつ]みを 用意[ようい] しています。
I prepared fourteen wrapped tea treats as souvenirs.
Counter,Somewhat Common
包み · つつみ · Wrapped things.
あの 患者[かんじゃ]さんは、 交通[こうつう] 事故[じこ]で ４[よん] 歯[は]を 欠損[けっそん] しているんですよ。
That patient lost four teeth in a car accident.
Counter,Somewhat Common
歯 · し · Teeth. In day-to-day life, it's more common to count teeth using the counter 本.
馬鹿[ばか]じゃない？
Are you crazy?
Emotion
どう して こんなに 馬鹿[ばか]だったのか？
How could I have been so stupid?
Emotion
謝[あやま]れ！
Apologize!
Emotion
感謝[かんしゃ] します。
I'm grateful. / I appreciate it.
Emotion
文句[もんく] あるのか？
Any complaints!?
Emotion
あなたは 清潔[せいけつ]。
You're clean. (physically, usually) クリーン (morals) (な政治家) or 精錬潔白
Emotion
あなたは 不潔[ふけつ]。
You're dirty.
Emotion
素晴[すば]らしいです！
Excellent!
鼠,Emotion
素晴しい
あなたに とても 興味[きょうみ]が あります。
I'm very interested in you.
Emotion
お弁当[べんとう]は 温[あたた]めますか？
Would you like to heat the bento?
Travel

A question asking if the bento should be heated. お弁当 (obento) means "bento," 温めます (atatamemasu) means "to warm up," and か (ka) turns it into a question. · When you purchase food at a convience store, it's common for the staff to ask if you would like it warmed up.
駅弁[えきべん]は どこで 買[か]えますか？
Where can I buy a train station lunch box?
鼠,Travel
新[しん]幹線[かんせん]の ホームは どこですか？
Where is the Shinkansen platform?
Travel

"新幹線" refers to the Shinkansen (bullet train), "の" indicates possession or relation, so "新幹線の" means "of the Shinkansen" or "Shinkansen's." "ホーム" means "platform." "は" is the topic particle, marking "ホーム" as the topic of the sentence, and "どこですか" asks "where is it?" in a polite form.
本[ほん]に 興味[きょうみ]を 持[も]つ
I'm interested in the book
鼠,Emotion
興味
折[お]り紙[がみ]で 5[ご] 弁[べん]の 花[はな]を 折[お]りました。
I made a five-petal origami flower.
Counter,Somewhat Common
弁 · べん · Petals that are still attached to a flower.
人生[じんせい]は なんて 素晴[すば]らしいんだろう。
Life is wonderful / what a wonderful life I have.
Emotion
素晴[すば]らしい 思[おも]い出[で]が たくさん できた。
You've given me many wonderful memories.
Emotion
新[しん]幹線[かんせん]の きっぷは どこで 買[か]えますか？
Where can I buy a Shinkansen ticket?
鼠,Travel
新[あたら]しい トーフグの ステッカーの アイディアを １０[じゅう] 案[あん] 提出[ていしゅつ] した。
I submitted ten new Tofugu sticker design ideas.
Counter,Somewhat Common

案 · あん · Plans, ideas, projects, and strategies. While you can also use the 〜つ counter to count these things, you'll probably hear 案 used more often in business situations. Count all 案 numbers with kango.
素直[すなお]な 性格[せいかく]の 人[ひと]
A person with an honest personality
鼠,Emotion
素直な
あなたは 悲観[ひかん] 主義[しゅぎ]者[しゃ]。
You're a pessimist.
Emotion
素晴[すば]らしい 家族[かぞく]を 築[きず]こう。
Let's make a wonderful family.
Emotion
本当[ほんとう]とは 思[おも]えないほど 素晴[すば]らしい
This is too good to be true.
Emotion
感謝[かんしゃ]の お礼[れい]を 受[う]け取[と]ってください。
Please accept this as a token of my appreciation.
Emotion
アヤは アメリカの 大統領[だいとうりょう]を ２[に]期[き] 務[つと]めた。
Aya served two terms as President of the United States.
Counter,Somewhat Common
期 · き · 期 is a fairly formal counter used to enumerate terms and periods.
新[しん]幹線[かんせん]の ひかり ４９３[よんひゃくきゅうじゅうさん]号[ごう]に 乗[の]りました。
I rode on the Shinkansen Hikari 493.
Counter,Somewhat Common
号 · ごう · 号 is an ordinal number suffix used for room numbers, train numbers, magazine volume numbers, and many other ordinal numbers. Inexplicably, it's also a unit for canvas sizes.
とても 美[うつく]しい 桜[さくら]の 花[はな]ですね。 １[いち] 枝[えだ] 分[わ]けてもらえませんか？
Such beautiful cherry blossoms. May I take a branch?
Counter,Somewhat Common

枝 · えだ · Branches with flowers, fruit, or elegant leaves on them. For bare branches, you can use the long stick Japanese counter 本 (ほん), and for one and two, count with the wago counting method. For the rest, use kango.
ご覧[らん] ください
Please take a look
Travel
This is a polite request. ご覧 (goran) is a polite form of the verb 見る (miru), meaning "to look," and ください (kudasai) is a polite way to ask for something.

No sugar, please
Travel
ご恩[おん]は 決[けっ]して 忘[わす]れません。
I'll never forget this favour.
Emotion
試合[しあい]に 興奮[こうふん] する
I get excited about the games.
鼠,Emotion
興奮
大変[たいへん] 申[もう]し訳[わけ] ございません。
I have absolutely no excuse.

これは 金閣[きんかく]寺[じ]と 言[い]います。
This is called the Kinkaku-ji.
鼠,Travel
あなたは 私[わたし]の 元気[げんき]の 素[もと]です。
You are the air that I breathe.
Emotion
1[いち]筋[すじ]の 希望[きぼう]が 見[み]えてきたぞ。
I'm starting to see a single ray of hope.
Counter,Somewhat Common
筋 · すじ · Line, stripe, streak, crease, crack, wrinkle, or avenue.
金閣[きんかく]寺[じ]は ここから 近[ちか]いですか？
Is Kinkaku-ji near here?
Travel
金閣寺 (きんかくじ, Kinkaku-ji) is the proper noun for the Golden Pavilion.
この 番組[ばんぐみ]から カップルが ３[さん]組[くみ] 誕生[たんじょう] した。
This show created three couples.
Counter,Common

組 · くみ · Set, a group, or a pair of something. For one and two groups, use the wago reading (ひとくみ、ふたくみ). Three can be either (みくみ or さんさら). From four on up, just use kango. Quite commonly, you'll see 組 used to categorize classrooms too. When it's used this way, you just use kango. One class will be named ４組 (fourth class group), another ８組 (eighth class group).
敵国[てきこく]の ３[さん] 軍[ぐん]が こちらへ 向[む]かっている そうだ。
I hear three enemy army troops are headed our way.
Counter,Somewhat Common
軍 · ぐん · Army groups, groups of troops, sports team levels, baseball team levels, etc.
今[いま]こそ 底力[そこぢから]を 発揮[はっき] すべき
Show right now me what you're made of!
Emotion
私[わたし]は 日系[にっけい] ブラジル人[じん] 3[さん]世[せい]です。
I'm a third-generation Japanese Brazilian.
Counter,Somewhat Common
世 · せい · Generations.
聖書[せいしょ]の 3[さん]節[せつ]を みんなで 暗証[あんしょう] した。
We recited three passages from the Bible together.
Counter,Somewhat Common
節 · せつ · Passages, sections, paragraphs, verses, clauses.
９[きゅう]院[いん]で 院内[いんない] 感染[かんせん]が 発生[はっせい] している。
The hospital-acquired infection has appeared in nine hospitals.
Counter,Somewhat Common

院 · いん · Organizations or institutions whose names end with 院, including hospitals (病院/びょういん), temples or mosques (寺院/じいん), government houses like 上院/じょういん (Upper House) or 下院/かいん (Lower House), etc. One exception is 美容院 (びよういん), beauty salons. Because they're shops, they're counted with 軒 (けん).
あなたは これまで 会[あ]った 中[なか]で 一番[いちばん]、 素敵[すてき]な 人[ひと]。
You're the most wonderful person I've ever met.
Emotion
俳句[はいく]は 五[ご] 文字[もじ]、 七[なな] 文字[もじ]、 五[ご] 文字[もじ]で 書[か]かないといけません。
You need to write haiku with a five-seven-five syllable count.
Counter,Common
文字 · もじ · Letters, characters, morae in poetry.

隣の (となりの, tonari no) means "next" or "neighboring," and ホーム (hōmu) means "platform."

こちらの 棚[たな]に おにぎりが あります。
The onigiri is on this shelf.
Travel
こちら (kochira) means "this (direction or place)," and the particle に (ni) indicates the location. が (ga) is the subject marker here, highlighting the onigiri as the subject.
みんなが 憧[あこが]れる ような カップルに なろう。

この ダイナーには テーブルが 3[さん] 卓[たく]しか ない。

卓 · たく · Tables, desks, Mahjong tables, dining tables, etc.

即日 (sokujitsu) means "same day," and つき (tsuki) means "available" or "included," referring to the time frame of availability.
喜[よろこ]びを 隠[かく]せない。

もう 頑張[がんば]りたくない。

選択[せんたく]の サービスが ありますか？

選択 (せんたく, sentaku) means "choice," and the sentence asks if such choices are available.
渋谷[しぶや]へは どう いったらいいですか？

ご愁傷[しゅうしょう]様[さま]です。
My condolences.
Emotion
今日[きょう]の お勧[すす]めは？
What is today’s recommendation?
Travel

今日の (きょうの, kyō no) means "today's," and the question word は (wa) marks the topic of the sentence, which is "today's recommendation." · You'll notice that this isn't a compelte sentence. The complete version of this sentence would be 今日のお勧めは何ですか？In Japanese it is very common to trail off and let the person you are talking to finish your sentnece with a response. It's strange for English speakers at first, but you'll get used to it over time.
